about.heading: I make hardware *think.*
paragraphs: I'm **Pavan Kumar Mathi**, a final-year B.Tech Electronics & Communication Engineering student at **MVGR College of Engineering**, Vizianagaram, graduating in 2027.

I like owning the whole stack. I wire the sensors, write the firmware in Embedded C, train the vision model, and run a local LLM on top, with no cloud needed. Right now I'm building **A.I.R**, an offline companion rover on the Arduino UNO Q, and **KAISER**, a personal AI agent with 41 tools and 365 automated tests.
On the side I ship real web apps for real businesses, like the live e-commerce site for a local fancy store.

items.title: A.I.R — Artificial Intelligence Rover
items.intro: An offline companion rover that sees, listens, talks and moves on its own. It runs on the Arduino UNO Q (Debian Linux plus an on-board MCU), so nothing goes to the cloud.
bullets: Trained a YOLOv8n object detector on 592 images; the AI "brain" picks a behaviour mode and the MCU drives the motors.
Local LLM (qwen2.5 1.5B on Ollama) for conversation, Moonshine speech-to-text and Piper text-to-speech.
Built a 2D house simulator where the real AI code drives a virtual MCU; fixed a stuck-in-corner bug down to 0 wall bumps in a 5-minute run.

items.title: KAISER — Personal AI Agent
items.intro: A JARVIS-style assistant that runs fully on my laptop. Say "Hey Kaiser" and it plans a task, asks before anything risky, runs it with real tools, checks the result and reports back.
bullets: 41 tools: writes, tests and fixes code; packages a Windows .exe; researches the web with citations; answers questions from PDFs.
Security first: Windows AppContainer sandbox, guarded browser (SSRF-safe), tamper-evident HMAC audit log, signed phone commands with a PIN.
Grew out of my earlier ZORO assistant and LoRA fine-tuning experiments on Qwen.

items.title: Disaster Response Decision Support
items.intro: Turns messy disaster reports (text and photos) into a ranked list of zones and a fair plan for sending rescue teams, ambulances and supplies, with a plain-English reason for each choice.
bullets: Fine-tuned DistilBERT on 15 humanitarian categories and ResNet50 on damage severity (CrisisNLP / CrisisMMD).
Found that blending text and image severity hurt accuracy, so redesigned it as two axes: damage and urgency.
PuLP linear programming for fair allocation, an LLM for explanations, a Streamlit dashboard.

items.title: Ladies Fancy Store — Online Shop
items.intro: A real e-commerce site for a local ladies fancy store, built and deployed for the owner. It runs as a catalogue today, and full ordering can be switched on from the admin panel when the shop is ready.
bullets: Flask + SQLAlchemy on Neon Postgres, deployed on Vercel with auto-deploy from GitHub.
Cart, checkout, Razorpay + cash on delivery, and pickup / local / courier delivery are all built in.
Admin panel for products, categories, orders and shop settings; red-gold theme with animations.

items.title: ESP32-CAM Surveillance Robot
items.intro: A Wi-Fi robot car that streams live video to a browser dashboard and drives from a phone or laptop. It's the hardware ancestor of A.I.R.
bullets: MJPEG live streaming from the ESP32-CAM with a web dashboard for movement and speed control.
Variable motor-speed (PWM) control and precise turning through the motor driver.
Next: on-board human detection and alerts with snapshot capture.
